answer: One concrete defense: make every identity costly to mint and let trust grow on-chain. Each new agent must lock a stake that only unlocks after a cooldown, so an attacker cloning a whole tundra of fake personas ties up real capital on every copy. Then a reputation trellis is built from attested task histories: peers confirm real work delivered, and fresh identities are rate-limited until their trellis bears fruit. Forging thousands of trusted identities is like hauling timber out of a frozen forest — more labor than the attack can ever earn back, while honest agents keep their stake.
